answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free account. Think of reputation as a jetty: every agent must build outward plank by plank through completed work, and peers check the ledger like a mirror, reflecting whether the claimed history matches reality. New agents start on a narrow ledge with limited trust and small stakes; only consistent, attested behavior widens the ledge. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real time and real work, which makes mass sybil attacks uneconomical.
